title: Numerical invariant and termination for marked ideals
statement:
Over $\mathbf Q$, a marked ideal is data $(Z,N,E,I,b)$: $Z$ and its closed subscheme $N$ are smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-closed-immersion], $E$ is a finite ordered list of smooth hypersurfaces meeting $N$ with normal crossings (locally their equations are distinct smooth coordinate parameters), $I\subset\mathcal O_N$ is coherent [pqf-def-coherent], and $b\ge1$ is an integer. Its cosupport is $\{x\in N:I_x\subset\mathfrak m_x^b\}$. Admissible blowups have smooth center in the cosupport transverse to $E$; transform $N$ strictly and divide the total transform of $I$ by the $b$th exceptional ideal. Test equivalence means equality of the admissible test sequences, also allowing products with a line and blowups of intersections of two exceptional hypersurfaces, with ordinary ideal pullback for those two operations [def-nagata-global-blowup, def-nagata-strict-transform].

There is one assignment, defined simultaneously for all such marked ideals over $\mathbf Q$ and all their admissible histories, of a finite lexicographic word at each point of the cosupport, with values in one fixed totally ordered set, made of rational residual orders, nonnegative integers counting earlier exceptional components, and a terminal monomial entry, such that the following hold; the companion/coefficient-ideal construction provides one. For a maximal-order marked ideal its first entry is $1$. The rest of the word, including the terminal tie-breaking data from the ordered exceptional components, is invariant under test equivalence for fixed dimension and under smooth pullback. The word has finite image on quasi-compact inputs and is upper semicontinuous. Its full maximum locus is a smooth closed center transverse to $E$. After blowing up this center the maximum word strictly decreases until cosupport is empty. The resulting process terminates, also when a finite number of equivalent local presentations are patched and the maximum is taken over their union. More precisely, at fixed leading data coefficient ideals reduce the smooth support dimension, and the final monomial case terminates by reduction of the ordered exponent data; thus an infinite tail with all earlier entries fixed is impossible. This is a theorem about marked ideals and their controlled transforms, not about strict transforms of arbitrary singular schemes.
